analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B remains a public-health priority in China, and intra-familial transmission from index cases to spouses contributes to ongoing transmission. The study aimed to quantify HBV seroprevalence and assess knowledge gaps among spouses of reported HBV cases to inform family-based prevention strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional survey was conducted in 2024 across three randomly selected counties in Quzhou City, enrolling spouses aged 18 years or older of HBV cases reported between January 2023 and September 2024.
analysis.methods: Participants completed a structured questionnaire on HBV knowledge and provided blood samples for serological testing of HBsAg, anti-HBs, anti-HBe, anti-HBc, and HBeAg. Multivariate logistic regression identified correlates of knowledge awareness.
analysis.main_results: Among 344 valid respondents, 161 provided blood samples; HBsAg positivity was 11.80%, anti-HBs 60.87%, anti-HBe 23.60%, anti-HBc 77.02%, and no participant tested positive for HBeAg. Overall HBV knowledge awareness was 36.69% with a pass rate of 22.09%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the high HBsAg prevalence and low knowledge as indicating substantial intra-familial transmission risk, and they highlight the need for targeted education, especially for older adults, farmers/workers, and those unaware of their infection status.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support family-focused interventions—health education, vaccination promotion, and regular testing—delivered through medical institutions and online platforms to reduce household transmission and improve HBV control.

Among 344 respondents, 161 provided blood samples, yielding an HBsAg positivity of 11.80% and serological evidence of past infection in 77.02%. Multivariate analysis linked lower knowledge to older age, farming/working occupations, and unawareness of personal infection status. The authors recommend targeted health education via hospitals and online platforms to promote vaccination and testing, aiming to curb intra-familial transmission.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 传播 仍然是中国的公共卫生重点,从指示病例到配偶的家庭内部 传播 有助于持续进行 传播。该研究旨在量化 HBV 血清流行率 并评估报告的 HBV 病例配偶之间的知识差距,为基于家庭的预防策略提供信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024年,在衢州市随机选择的三个县开展了一项横断面调查,纳入了2023年1月至2024年9月期间报告的乙型肝炎病例的18岁及以上配偶。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将高HBV感染率和低知识水平解读为家庭内传播风险显著,并强调需针对老年人、农民/工人及不了解自身感染状况者开展有针对性的健康教育。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 横截面设计和对自我报告数据的依赖限制了因果推断,并可能低估 患病率;由于潜在的选择和信息偏差以及缺乏基因型或病毒载量数据,证据是中等的。

papers.title: Hepatitis B vaccine-induced immunity among hill tribe and stateless children in northern Thailand
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to determine the difference in seroprotection between fully and partially vaccinated hill tribe and stateless children aged five years in northern Thailand along with the factors associated with the absence of anti-HBs in these children since vaccine implementation began in 1992. A case–control study was conducted to collect information from hill tribe and stateless individuals living in villages in Mae Fah Luang District, Chiang Rai Province. Children with no prior immunization, delayed immunization, or incomplete hepatitis B vaccination were included. Children who were completely vaccinated were included as controls. A questionnaire was distributed and 3 mL blood samples were collected for the qualitative and quantitative detection of hepatitis B biomarkers. Logistic regression was applied to detect factors associated with the absence of anti-HBs. A total of 188 cases and 188 controls were included in the study; 54% were male, and 54.3% belonged to the Akha group. The overall prevalence of anti-HBs was 59.3%; 55.3% of anti-HBs was detected in children with complete vaccination (with 2 children positive for anti-HBc), and 55.3% was detected in children with incomplete vaccination. Children whose birth weight was <2500 g (AOR = 3.52; 95% CI = 1.39–9.12), whose mother belonged to the Yao group (AOR = 16.90; 95% CI = 2.00–142.57), whose mother practiced Christianity (AOR = 2.30; 95% CI = 1.18–4.46), and whose father was aged 30–39 years (AOR = 2.20; 95% CI = 1.01–4.80) were more likely to exhibit an absence of anti-HBs. The hepatitis B vaccine-induced immune response rate among hill tribe and stateless children remains undesirable, and an effective assessment program is needed to monitor this issue.

papers.source_body_en: The aim of this study was to determine the difference in seroprotection between fully and partially vaccinated hill tribe and stateless children aged five years in northern Thailand along with the factors associated with the absence of anti-HBs in these children since vaccine implementation began in 1992. A case–control study was conducted to collect information from hill tribe and stateless individuals living in villages in Mae Fah Luang District, Chiang Rai Province. A questionnaire was distributed and 3 mL blood samples were collected for the qualitative and quantitative detection of hepatitis B biomarkers. The hepatitis B vaccine-induced immune response rate among hill tribe and stateless children remains undesirable, and an effective assessment program is needed to monitor this issue.

papers.title: Hepatitis B Virus Infection: a Comprehensive Review of Viral Biology, Clinical Spectrum, and Preventive Strategies
papers.abstract: Infection with hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a serious health issue around the world, and one of the most common causes of long-term liver problems such as chronic liver disease and cirrhosis, and liver cancer. HBV is caused by the hepatitis B virus, which is part of the family of viruses called Hepadnaviridae and consists of a partially double-stranded DNA genome. Transmission occurs primarily through the exchange of blood and body fluids. The objective of this study was to collect available information about HBV infections and assess that information with respect to the following areas: epidemiology of HBV infection, viral biology, clinical features of HBV infection, diagnosis and treatment of HBV infection, and prevention of HBV infection. This study is a descriptive literature review based on the secondary research data acquired from the World Health Organization (WHO), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and peer-reviewed literature. A qualitative analysis process was used to extract the relevant information contained in the published literature. There are many different types of HBV infections. There are individuals who are asymptomatic carriers of HBV; individuals who have an acute HBV infection; individuals with chronic HBV infection; and individuals with cirrhosis and/or liver cancer caused by HBV. The diagnosis of HBV infection is determined by the presence of serological markers associated with the infection, such as HBsAg, HBeAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs, and HBV DNA levels. These markers also assist in determining whether or not the individual is infectious and how far progressed the disease is. Antiviral therapies available for treating HBV infection include tenofovir and entecavir which have been shown to effectively suppress viral replication but are unable to eliminate the covalently closed circular (ccc) DNA of the virus. Vaccination against HBV has demonstrated a reduction in the incident cases and remains the most effective means of prevention. The burden of HBV infection as a preventable global health issue continues. Properly diagnosing someone infected with HBV, treating the individual with an antiviral agent, and providing universal vaccination will be necessary to decrease the morbidity and mortality associated with HBV infection.

papers.title: Characterising Hepatitis D Virus in the UK From 2011 to 2021.
papers.abstract: Little is known about hepatitis B virus (HBV) and Hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection in the UK. HDV screening is recommended among all individuals with HBV, with coinfection associated with increased disease progression. Using data on HDV testing, shared by 11 laboratories in the UK who reported undertaking HDV testing, and national testing data for HBV we established a cohort of individuals tested for HDV, investigating testing pathways, describing characteristics and outcomes of those HDV-RNA positive to inform targeted interventions for testing, diagnosis and linkage to care. Demographic information, clinical assessments, treatment and recent laboratory results from NHS trusts, and through linkage to national healthcare datasets was collected for HDV-RNA positive individuals. Between 2011 and 2021, 42% of individuals newly diagnosed with HBV in England were linked to an HDV test. Anti-HDV positivity was 5.0%, 55.8% were HDV-RNA tested and 45.7% were ever HDV-RNA positive. HDV-RNA positivity in the absence of an anti-HDV result was 6.4%. Among individuals who were HDV-RNA positive, 94.3% were non-UK born, with 24 different primary languages reported, 49% had evidence of treatment, and 48% had evidence of cirrhosis. 10% had died of which 58.4% died of liver disease. In conclusion, our findings indicate that HDV testing in HBV positive individuals in the UK is sub-optimal against testing guidelines, including RNA testing among those who are anti-HDV positive. Considerable work is needed to improve the patient care pathway, to ensure patients are appropriately diagnosed, linked and retained in care, with adequate access to treatment.

It found that only 42% of newly diagnosed HBV cases were linked to HDV testing, with 5.0% anti-HDV positivity and 45.7% ever HDV-RNA positive among those tested. papers.title_zh: 2011 年至 2021 年英国丁型肝炎病毒的特征。
papers.source_body_en: Little is known about hepatitis B virus (HBV) and Hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection in the UK. HDV screening is recommended among all individuals with HBV, with coinfection associated with increased disease progression. Using data on HDV testing, shared by 11 laboratories in the UK who reported undertaking HDV testing, and national testing data for HBV we established a cohort of individuals tested for HDV, investigating testing pathways, describing characteristics and outcomes of those HDV-RNA positive to inform targeted interventions for testing, diagnosis and linkage to care. Demographic information, clinical assessments, treatment and recent laboratory results from NHS trusts, and through linkage to national healthcare datasets was collected for HDV-RNA positive individuals. Between 2011 and 2021, 42% of individuals newly diagnosed with HBV in England were linked to an HDV test. Anti-HDV positivity was 5.0%, 55.8% were HDV-RNA tested and 45.7% were ever HDV-RNA positive. HDV-RNA positivity in the absence of an anti-HDV result was 6.4%. Among individuals who were HDV-RNA positive, 94.3% were non-UK born, with 24 different primary languages reported, 49% had evidence of treatment, and 48% had evidence of cirrhosis. 10% had died of which 58.4% died of liver disease. In conclusion, our findings indicate that HDV testing in HBV positive individuals in the UK is sub-optimal against testing guidelines, including RNA testing among those who are anti-HDV positive. Considerable work is needed to improve the patient care pathway, to ensure patients are appropriately diagnosed, linked and retained in care, with adequate access to treatment.
papers.abstract_zh: 在英国,人们对 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 和丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 的双重感染知之甚少。建议对所有 HBV 感染者进行 HDV 筛查,因为合并感染会导致疾病进展加快。利用英国 11 个报告进行 HDV 检测的实验室共享的 HDV 检测数据以及全国 HBV 检测数据,我们建立了 HDV 检测个体的 队列研究,调查检测途径,描述 HDV-RNA 阳性的特征和结果,为检测、诊断 和护理联系的针对性干预措施提供信息。我们收集了 HDV-RNA 阳性个体的人口统计信息、临床评估、治疗 和 NHS 信托机构的最新实验室结果,并通过与国家医疗保健数据集的链接来收集。2011 年至 2021 年间,英格兰新诊断出的 HBV 患者中有 42% 与 HDV 检测有关。抗 HDV 阳性率为 5.0%,55.8% 进行过 HDV-RNA 检测,45.7% 曾经呈 HDV-RNA 阳性。在没有抗 HDV 结果的情况下,HDV-RNA 阳性率为 6.4%。在 HDV-RNA 阳性的个体中,94.3% 为非英国出生,报告有 24 种不同的主要语言,49% 有 治疗 证据,48% 有肝硬化证据。10%的人死于肝病,其中58.4%死于肝病。总之,我们的研究结果表明,在英国,针对 HBV 阳性个体的 HDV 检测相对于检测指南(包括抗 HDV 阳性者的 RNA 检测)来说并不是最佳的。需要做大量的工作来改善患者护理途径,以确保患者得到适当的诊断、联系和保留护理,并有足够的机会获得 治疗。

papers.title: Hepatitis B and D burden in Uzbekistan: comprehensive analysis of seroprevalence and risk correlates from a countrywide study
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Uzbekistan faces a substantial burden of hepatitis B and D virus (HBV and HDV) infections despite implementing universal hepatitis B vaccination in 1998. Regional variation in disease distribution and contemporary transmission dynamics remain inadequately characterized. Our objective was to evaluate the geographically stratified prevalence of HBV and HDV, while also identifying the key risk factors fueling transmission within the adult population of Uzbekistan. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional study of 10,552 adults across seven regions of Uzbekistan from July 2022 to June 2024. Participants were selected using stratified random sampling from a parent cohort of 1,048,575 individuals. Serological testing included hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), antibodies to hepatitis B core antigen (anti-HBc), anti-HDV antibodies, and viral RNA detection. Multivariate logistic regression identified independent risk factors for HBV and HDV infections. RESULTS: Overall HBsAg prevalence was 4.7% (95% CI: 4.3-5.1%), with substantial geographic heterogeneity ranging from 3.2% in Tashkent to 6.3% in Bukhara. Among HBsAg-positive individuals, 68.1% had detectable HBV DNA and 12.7% had HDV superinfection. HDV RNA prevalence among HBV DNA-positive individuals ranged from 2.5% to 23.7% across regions. Age-cohort analysis demonstrated vaccination program impact, with older unvaccinated adults bearing disproportionate disease burden. Female sex associated with 31% lower odds of chronic HBsAg carriage. Married status, healthcare-associated exposures, and body piercings correlated with increased anti-HBc positivity. Remarkably, sharing personal hygiene items showed striking HDV-specific association (aOR 2.34, 95% CI: 1.16-4.74; P = 0.02) but no association with HBV markers, suggesting distinct transmission pathways for HDV superinfection. CONCLUSIONS: Persistent HBV burden with notable regional clustering and HDV superinfection necessitates targeted interventions. The identification of personal hygiene item sharing as a specific HDV transmission route provides an actionable household-level prevention target. Intensified screening and treatment of unvaccinated adults remain critical for hepatitis elimination efforts.

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 横断面设计限制了因果推断,并且依赖血清学标志物可能会低估隐匿性乙型肝炎病毒感染;然而,大量的地理分层样本和稳健的统计方法强化了证据。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 尽管自 1998 年以来乌兹别克斯坦在全国范围内实施了 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染,但乌兹别克斯坦仍然承受着巨大的 传播 (HBV) 感染负担,而且对疾病分布和 传播 动态的区域差异仍知之甚少。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 2022 年 7 月至 2024 年 6 月在乌兹别克斯坦进行了一项全国性横断面研究,通过分层随机抽样从七个地区的 1,048,575 名个体的父母 队列研究 中筛选出 10,552 名成年人。
analysis_zh.methods: 血清学检测包括乙型肝炎表面抗原(HBsAg)、乙型肝炎核心抗原抗体(抗-HBc)和病毒RNA检测,并使用多变量逻辑回归来识别乙型肝炎病毒感染的独立危险因素。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持对未接种疫苗的成年人加强筛查和 治疗 以及有针对性的家庭预防措施,特别是 HDV 传播,以推进乌兹别克斯坦消除肝炎的努力。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 横断面设计限制了因果推断,并且依赖血清学标志物可能会低估隐匿性乙型肝炎病毒感染;然而,大量的地理分层样本和稳健的统计方法强化了证据。

papers.title: Development and validation of GADA model for diagnosing hepatocellular carcinoma in Chinese hepatitis B patients.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection accounts for more than 40% of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cases worldwide. The GALAD (Gender, Age, alpha fetoprotein heterogeneity [AFP-L3], AFP, and des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin [PIVKA-II/DCP]) model has potential for enhancing HCC diagnosis. However, its diagnostic performance in HBV-associated chronic liver disease requires further optimization. This study aimed to establish a diagnostic model for HBV-associated HCC. METHODS: The data from 2190 patients with HBV-related liver diseases, including chronic hepatitis B (CHB), cirrhosis, and HCC were analysed. The GADA model was developed by omitting AFP-L3 for improved accessibility, and its performance was assessed via the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Validation was performed on 20,908 patients across ten hospitals. RESULTS: The simplified GADA model demonstrated exceptional diagnostic performance in identifying HBV-related HCC in the modeling group, achieving an AUC of 0.940 (95% CI, 0.927-0.952), with a sensitivity and specificity of 82.57% and 91.53%, respectively, surpassing the original GALAD model's AUC of 0.907 (95% CI, 0.891-0.921). In the internal validation cohort, the GADA model had an AUC of 0.935 (95% CI, 0.914-0.953), sensitivity of 82.04%, and specificity of 92.65%. For early-stage HCC detection, the AUC in the modeling group was 0.858 (95% CI, 0.837-0.877), and in the internal validation group was 0.868 (95% CI, 0.836-0.895), significantly better than the original GALAD model. External validation with 20,908 participants yielded an AUC of 0.919 (95% CI, 0.916-0.923), with sensitivity of 86.00% and specificity 81.88%. For early-stage HCC diagnosis, the AUC was 0.903 (95% CI: 0.898-0.907), with sensitivity of 88.16% and specificity 74.50%. CONCLUSIONS: The GADA model shows exceptional promise for diagnosing HBV-related HCC, enhancing early detection and reducing misdiagnosis rates. Its clinical utility is supported by robust validation, indicating significant implications for patient prognosis and treatment options.

papers.title_zh: 用于诊断中国乙型肝炎患者肝细胞癌的 GADA 模型的开发和验证。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection accounts for more than 40% of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cases worldwide. The GALAD (Gender, Age, alpha fetoprotein heterogeneity [AFP-L3], AFP, and des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin [PIVKA-II/DCP]) model has potential for enhancing HCC diagnosis. However, its diagnostic performance in HBV-associated chronic liver disease requires further optimization. This study aimed to establish a diagnostic model for HBV-associated HCC. METHODS: The data from 2190 patients with HBV-related liver diseases, including chronic hepatitis B (CHB), cirrhosis, and HCC were analysed. The GADA model was developed by omitting AFP-L3 for improved accessibility, and its performance was assessed via the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Validation was performed on 20,908 patients across ten hospitals. RESULTS: The simplified GADA model demonstrated exceptional diagnostic performance in identifying HBV-related HCC in the modeling group, achieving an AUC of 0.940 (95% CI, 0.927-0.952), with a sensitivity and specificity of 82.57% and 91.53%, respectively, surpassing the original GALAD model's AUC of 0.907 (95% CI, 0.891-0.921). In the internal validation cohort, the GADA model had an AUC of 0.935 (95% CI, 0.914-0.953), sensitivity of 82.04%, and specificity of 92.65%. For early-stage HCC detection, the AUC in the modeling group was 0.858 (95% CI, 0.837-0.877), and in the internal validation group was 0.868 (95% CI, 0.836-0.895), significantly better than the original GALAD model. External validation with 20,908 participants yielded an AUC of 0.919 (95% CI, 0.916-0.923), with sensitivity of 86.00% and specificity 81.88%. For early-stage HCC diagnosis, the AUC was 0.903 (95% CI: 0.898-0.907), with sensitivity of 88.16% and specificity 74.50%. CONCLUSIONS: The GADA model shows exceptional promise for diagnosing HBV-related HCC, enhancing early detection and reducing misdiagnosis rates. Its clinical utility is supported by robust validation, indicating significant implications for patient prognosis and treatment options.

papers.title: Deep Sequencing of Hepatitis B Virus Reveals Clinically Relevant Low-Frequency Variants Among People Living with HIV in Botswana
papers.abstract: (1) Background: The Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is characterized by extensive genetic diversity, including low-frequency variants that contribute to disease progression. We aimed to characterize low-frequency variants and evaluate their potential clinical impact. (2) Methods: We utilized 104 HBV near-full-length sequences generated using next-generation sequencing (NGS) from people living with HIV (PLHIV). We used an in-house bioinformatics suite (HBVgenomeR v5.9.7) to filter for low-frequency variants (5–50%), which were compared to escape and drug resistance mutations (DRMs) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)-associated mutations reported at the consensus level. Unclassified variants were characterized by HBV open reading frames (ORFs) to determine mutation frequency per genomic region. (3) Results: A total of six escape mutations were detected in 8/104 (7.7%) sequences, with surfaceN131T being the most prevalent (5/8). We also observed six DRMs in 30/104 (28.8%), with rtV173L being the most prevalent (21/30). Truncation mutations were also observed with rtA181T/sW172* and rtM204I/sW196L being the most prevalent. A total of 8/104 (7.7%) sequences had four variants associated with HCC. The xP46S was the highest observed HCC-associated mutation at 5/8. We report 1152 unique uncharacterized variants across all ORFs, and these were found in 94/104 (90.4%) sequences. The RNaseH domain had the highest burden (330/1152, 28.6%). (4) Conclusions: Deep sequencing results identified clinically significant mutations, including those below the 20% detection limit of traditional sequencing, that would go unreported. This highlights the possible underreporting of mutational burden in people living with HBV/HIV, indicating the importance of deep sequencing to aid in HBV/HIV understanding and management.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterized low-frequency Hepatitis B virus (HBV) variants in people living with HIV (PLHIV) in Botswana using next-generation sequencing (NGS). Among 104 near-full-length HBV sequences, six escape mutations were detected in 7.7% of samples, six drug resistance mutations (DRMs) in 28.8%, and four hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)-associated variants in 7.7%. Truncation mutations and 1152 unique uncharacterized variants were also identified, with the RNaseH domain showing the highest mutational burden. The authors highlight that deep sequencing reveals clinically significant mutations below the 20% detection threshold of traditional methods, which may otherwise go unreported. These findings underscore the potential underreporting of HBV mutational burden in PLHIV and emphasize the value of deep sequencing for improving HBV/HIV management. papers.source_body_en: (1) Background: The Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is characterized by extensive genetic diversity, including low-frequency variants that contribute to disease progression. We aimed to characterize low-frequency variants and evaluate their potential clinical impact. (2) Methods: We utilized 104 HBV near-full-length sequences generated using next-generation sequencing (NGS) from people living with HIV (PLHIV). We used an in-house bioinformatics suite (HBVgenomeR v5.9.7) to filter for low-frequency variants (5–50%), which were compared to escape and drug resistance mutations (DRMs) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)-associated mutations reported at the consensus level. Unclassified variants were characterized by HBV open reading frames (ORFs) to determine mutation frequency per genomic region. A total of 8/104 (7.7%) sequences had four variants associated with HCC. The xP46S was the highest observed HCC-associated mutation at 5/8. We report 1152 unique uncharacterized variants across all ORFs, and these were found in 94/104 (90.4%) sequences. The RNaseH domain had the highest burden (330/1152, 28.6%). (4) Conclusions: Deep sequencing results identified clinically significant mutations, including those below the 20% detection limit of traditional sequencing, that would go unreported. papers.title: Antiviral profile of hepatitis B virus capsid assembly modulator ALG-001075, the parent of pevifoscorvir sodium.
papers.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains an important unmet medical need with 240 million patients worldwide. The HBV capsid assembly process has emerged as a key target for more efficient antiviral intervention. Pevifoscorvir sodium (ALG-000184), an oral prodrug of the potent HBV capsid assembly modulator (CAM) ALG-001075 showed significant reductions in HBV DNA, HBV RNA and other viral antigens (HBsAg, HBcrAg and HBeAg) in Phase I clinical participants with chronic HBV infection. We aim to characterize the antiviral properties of ALG-001075. ALG-001075 is a highly potent CAM that inhibited HBV DNA production in cellular settings with EC50 values below 1 nM and an EC99.9 value of only 22 nM. ALG-001075 was shown to induce the formation of empty, but not aberrant viral particles as demonstrated by fluorescence quenching, electron microscopy, size-exclusion chromatography, immunofluorescent staining and NMR analysis, thereby classifying it as a CAM-E. Notably, solid-state NMR spectra of wild-type capsids in the presence of ALG-001075 revealed a characteristic CAM-E fingerprint at atomic resolution. ALG-001075 showed potent antiviral activity against HBV strains from genotypes A-J, nucleoside analogue-resistant virus strains and known CAM-resistance mutations, with the exception of T33N, T33P and V124G, which induced 6-to-28-fold loss in ALG-001075 activity. The in vivo efficacy of ALG-001075 was confirmed in adeno-associated virus-HBV mice, where ALG-001075 demonstrated up to 5 log10 reduction in circulating HBV DNA levels. Because of its robust antiviral potency and favorable preclinical resistance profile, ALG-001075 was selected for further clinical development under the form of its prodrug pevifoscorvir sodium.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection represents a major global health burden with 240 million patients worldwide and limited therapeutic options. The study addresses the unmet need for more effective antiviral interventions by targeting the HBV capsid assembly process, which is critical for viral replication.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study characterizes the antiviral properties of the HBV capsid assembly modulator ALG-001075, the parent compound of pevifoscorvir sodium. It synthesizes preclinical data including cellular models, structural analyses, and in vivo efficacy studies in adeno-associated virus-HBV mice.
analysis.methods: ALG-001075 was evaluated for antiviral potency using cellular assays to determine EC50 and EC99.9 values. Structural characterization involved fluorescence quenching, electron microscopy, size-exclusion chromatography, immunofluorescent staining, NMR analysis, and solid-state NMR spectroscopy. In vivo efficacy was assessed in adeno-associated virus-HBV mice.
analysis.main_results: ALG-001075 demonstrated potent antiviral activity with EC50 values below 1 nM and an EC99.9 value of 22 nM. It induced the formation of empty viral particles without aberrant structures and produced a characteristic CAM-E fingerprint in solid-state NMR spectra. The compound showed activity against HBV genotypes A-J, nucleoside analogue-resistant strains, and most CAM-resistance mutations, except T33N, T33P, and V124G. In vivo, ALG-001075 achieved up to a 5 log10 reduction in circulating HBV DNA levels in mice.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish ALG-001075 as a highly potent and mechanistically distinct HBV capsid assembly modulator (CAM-E) with a favorable resistance profile. The atomic-resolution structural fingerprint and broad genotypic coverage represent novel contributions to HBV antiviral development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results support the clinical advancement of ALG-001075 as a promising therapeutic candidate for chronic HBV infection, particularly against resistant strains and diverse genotypes. Its potent antiviral activity and mechanistic specificity may inform future treatment strategies and resistance surveillance.

The strength of evidence is moderate due to the absence of comprehensive methodological and outcome reporting.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterizes ALG-001075, a potent hepatitis B virus (HBV) capsid assembly modulator (CAM) and the parent compound of pevifoscorvir sodium, addressing the unmet need for improved HBV therapies. The compound exhibits exceptional antiviral potency with EC50 values below 1 nM and an EC99.9 of 22 nM, inducing the formation of empty viral particles without aberrant structures. Structural analyses via NMR and microscopy reveal a distinct CAM-E fingerprint at atomic resolution. ALG-001075 demonstrates broad activity across HBV genotypes A-J, nucleoside analogue-resistant strains, and most CAM-resistance mutations, with reduced efficacy against T33N, T33P, and V124G. In vivo efficacy is confirmed in adeno-associated virus-HBV mice, where the compound achieves up to a 5 log10 reduction in HBV DNA. These findings support its clinical development as a mechanistically novel and potent antiviral for chronic HBV infection.

papers.source_body_en: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains an important unmet medical need with 240 million patients worldwide. The HBV capsid assembly process has emerged as a key target for more efficient antiviral intervention. Pevifoscorvir sodium (ALG-000184), an oral prodrug of the potent HBV capsid assembly modulator (CAM) ALG-001075 showed significant reductions in HBV DNA, HBV RNA and other viral antigens (HBsAg, HBcrAg and HBeAg) in Phase I clinical participants with chronic HBV infection. We aim to characterize the antiviral properties of ALG-001075. ALG-001075 is a highly potent CAM that inhibited HBV DNA production in cellular settings with EC50 values below 1 nM and an EC99.9 value of only 22 nM. ALG-001075 was shown to induce the formation of empty, but not aberrant viral particles as demonstrated by fluorescence quenching, electron microscopy, size-exclusion chromatography, immunofluorescent staining and NMR analysis, thereby classifying it as a CAM-E. Notably, solid-state NMR spectra of wild-type capsids in the presence of ALG-001075 revealed a characteristic CAM-E fingerprint at atomic resolution. ALG-001075 showed potent antiviral activity against HBV strains from genotypes A-J, nucleoside analogue-resistant virus strains and known CAM-resistance mutations, with the exception of T33N, T33P and V124G, which induced 6-to-28-fold loss in ALG-001075 activity. The in vivo efficacy of ALG-001075 was confirmed in adeno-associated virus-HBV mice, where ALG-001075 demonstrated up to 5 log10 reduction in circulating HBV DNA levels. Because of its robust antiviral potency and favorable preclinical resistance profile, ALG-001075 was selected for further clinical development under the form of its prodrug pevifoscorvir sodium.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究表征了 HBV 衣壳组装调节剂 ALG-001075(pevifoscorvir 钠的母体化合物)的 抗病毒药物 特性。它综合了临床前数据,包括细胞模型、结构分析和腺相关病毒-HBV 小鼠的体内功效研究。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用细胞测定法评估 ALG-001075 的 抗病毒药物 效力,以确定 EC50 和 EC99.9 值。结构表征涉及荧光猝灭、电子显微镜、尺寸排阻色谱、免疫荧光染色、NMR 分析和固态 NMR 光谱。在腺相关病毒-HBV 小鼠中评估体内功效。
analysis_zh.main_results: ALG-001075 表现出有效的 抗病毒药物 活性,EC50 值低于 1 nM,EC99.9 值为 22 nM。它诱导形成没有异常结构的空病毒颗粒,并在固态 NMR 光谱中产生特征性 CAM-E 指纹。该化合物对 HBV 基因型 A-J、核苷类似物耐药菌株和大多数 CAM 耐药菌株 突变(T33N、T33P 和 V124G 除外)表现出活性。在体内,ALG-001075 使小鼠循环 HBV DNA 水平降低了 5 log10。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明 ALG-001075 是一种高效且机制独特的 HBV 衣壳组装调节剂 (CAM-E),具有良好的耐药性。原子分辨率的结构指纹和广泛的基因型覆盖代表了对 HBV 抗病毒药物 开发的新贡献。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果支持 ALG-001075 作为慢性 HBV 感染的有前途的治疗候选药物的临床进展,特别是针对耐药菌株和不同基因型。其强大的 抗病毒药物 活性和机制特异性可能会为未来的 治疗 策略和耐药性 监测 提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于摘要中总结的临床前和早期临床数据,没有报告有关研究设计、样本量或统计分析的详细信息。由于缺乏全面的方法和结果报告,证据的强度中等。

papers.title: Molecular Characterization and Genotypic Distribution of Hepatitis B Virus Isolates in Iraq: Prevalence of Drug Resistance Mutations
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains one of the most pervasive viral threats worldwide, posing a significant risk to millions. Due to the absence of proofreading activity during reverse transcription, HBV exhibits a high genetic variability. To date, ten distinct HBV genotypes have been identified globally, associated with varying disease outcomes, including progression to cirrhosis and carcinoma, as well as responses to antivirals. Consequently, genotypic analysis and molecular characterization of HBV are critical for optimizing therapeutic strategies. This study aimed to investigate the distribution of HBV genotypes among Iraqi patients and to characterize their molecular profiles. Therefore, a modified protocol was used to improve sequencing success rates in samples with low amplification yields. Results: HBV/D was predominant in the study cohort (100%). Subgenotypic analysis revealed that HBV/D1 accounts for the majority of cases (68%), followed by D3 (32%). Sequences of 16 isolates were deposited in NCBI under accession numbers PV068280; PV124387–PV124397; and PV172617–PV172620. Moreover, the analysis of antiviral resistance indicated that 47% (32/68) of HBV/D1 isolates exhibited drug resistance, with all resistant isolates showing mutations associated with Lamivudine resistance (100%), Entecavir intermediate/high resistance (81% and 19%, respectively), and Telbivudine (25%). These findings underscore the dominance of genotype D, particularly HBV/D1 among Iraqi patients. To our knowledge, this is the first local study to correlate genotypic variation with drug resistance and highlight the importance of continuous surveillance for antiviral resistance to guide effective treatment strategies.

papers.title_zh: 伊拉克 乙型肝炎病毒 分离株的分子特征和基因型分布:患病率 的耐药性 突变
papers.source_body_en: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains one of the most pervasive viral threats worldwide, posing a significant risk to millions. Due to the absence of proofreading activity during reverse transcription, HBV exhibits a high genetic variability. To date, ten distinct HBV genotypes have been identified globally, associated with varying disease outcomes, including progression to cirrhosis and carcinoma, as well as responses to antivirals. Consequently, genotypic analysis and molecular characterization of HBV are critical for optimizing therapeutic strategies. This study aimed to investigate the distribution of HBV genotypes among Iraqi patients and to characterize their molecular profiles. Therefore, a modified protocol was used to improve sequencing success rates in samples with low amplification yields. Results: HBV/D was predominant in the study cohort (100%). Subgenotypic analysis revealed that HBV/D1 accounts for the majority of cases (68%), followed by D3 (32%). Sequences of 16 isolates were deposited in NCBI under accession numbers PV068280; PV124387–PV124397; and PV172617–PV172620. Moreover, the analysis of antiviral resistance indicated that 47% (32/68) of HBV/D1 isolates exhibited drug resistance, with all resistant isolates showing mutations associated with Lamivudine resistance (100%), Entecavir intermediate/high resistance (81% and 19%, respectively), and Telbivudine (25%). These findings underscore the dominance of genotype D, particularly HBV/D1 among Iraqi patients. To our knowledge, this is the first local study to correlate genotypic variation with drug resistance and highlight the importance of continuous surveillance for antiviral resistance to guide effective treatment strategies.

papers.title: The Uncared-for Carers: A Cross-Sectional Study of Hepatitis B Vaccination Uptake and Predictors Among Volunteer Healthcare Workers in Zambia: HBV Vaccination Uptake Among Volunteer HCWs.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) poses a major occupational risk to healthcare workers (HCWs), particularly in moderate-to-high‐prevalence settings such as Zambia. Despite the availability of a safe and effective vaccine, coverage among HCWs remains suboptimal. Among HCWs, volunteer HCWs face unique challenges, including financial barriers, that increase their risk. However, they are often overlooked in research. The present study aimed to determine HBV vaccination uptake and its predictors among volunteer HCWs in Zambia. METHODS: This national cross-sectional study utilized a self-administered semi-structured online questionnaire to collect data from volunteer HCWs from October 3 to November 26 2024. Using R version 4.6.0 and Stata version 17, descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were performed. A two-sided p value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. RESULTS: Among the 173 participants, 51 (29.5%) reported being vaccinated. Of the 51, 23 (45.1%) had received one dose, 4 (7.8%) two doses, and 24 (47.1%) at least three doses (fully vaccinated). In the multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression model, participants who had access to HBV vaccination programs during training were significantly more likely to be vaccinated than those without such programs (p < 0.001). Availability of HBV testing services at the health facility was also independently associated with vaccination uptake (p = 0.006). Increasing age was associated with slightly higher odds of vaccination (p = 0.025). Gender and place of education were not independently associated with vaccination uptake after adjustment. CONCLUSION: HBV vaccination coverage among volunteer HCWs in Zambia was low. Vaccination programs during training, age and the availability of HBV testing services were important factors associated with vaccine uptake. Strengthening institutional HBV prevention programs may improve vaccination coverage and reduce occupational risk among HCWs.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Occupational exposure to hepatitis B virus (HBV) places healthcare workers (HCWs) at elevated risk, yet vaccination coverage remains suboptimal despite the availability of a safe and effective vaccine. Volunteer HCWs face unique barriers such as financial constraints and are often overlooked in research, creating a knowledge gap about their vaccination status and determinants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A national cross-sectional study was conducted among volunteer HCWs in Zambia using a self-administered semi-structured online questionnaire administered from October 3 to November 26, 2024. The study included 173 participants and aimed to assess HBV vaccination uptake and its predictors.
analysis.methods: Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics with R version 4.6.0 and Stata version 17, applying a two-sided p value threshold of less than 0.05 for statistical significance. A multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression model was used to identify independent predictors of vaccination uptake.
analysis.main_results: Among 173 participants, 51 (29.5%) reported being vaccinated; of these, 23 (45.1%) had received one dose, 4 (7.8%) two doses, and 24 (47.1%) at least three doses (fully vaccinated). Access to HBV vaccination programs during training was significantly associated with vaccination (p < 0.001), as was the availability of HBV testing services at the health facility (p = 0.006). Increasing age was also associated with higher odds of vaccination (p = 0.025), while gender and place of education were not independently associated after adjustment.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights low HBV vaccination coverage among volunteer HCWs in Zambia and identifies institutional and demographic factors—vaccination programs during training, age, and on-site HBV testing services—as key determinants of uptake. This underscores the need for targeted interventions within training and facility-based prevention programs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that strengthening HBV vaccination programs during training and improving access to on-site testing services could substantially increase vaccination coverage among volunteer HCWs, thereby reducing occupational HBV infection risk in Zambia.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and reliance on self-reported vaccination status may introduce recall bias. The sample size of 173 participants and single-country setting further constrain generalizability, warranting cautious interpretation of the evidence strength as moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study assessed hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination uptake and predictors among 173 volunteer healthcare workers (HCWs) in Zambia using an online questionnaire administered from October to November 2024. Only 29.5% reported vaccination, with 47.1% of vaccinated participants fully immunized. Access to vaccination programs during training (p < 0.001) and availability of HBV testing services at health facilities (p = 0.006) were independently associated with higher uptake, as was increasing age (p = 0.025). Gender and place of education showed no independent association. The authors conclude that HBV vaccination coverage among volunteer HCWs is low and recommend strengthening institutional prevention programs to improve uptake and reduce occupational risk.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 职业接触 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 使医护人员 (HCW) 面临较高的风险,但尽管有安全有效的 疫苗,但 疫苗接种 的覆盖率仍然不理想。志愿医护人员面临着独特的障碍,例如财务限制,并且在研究中经常被忽视,从而造成了关于他们的 疫苗接种 状态和决定因素的知识差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024 年 10 月 3 日至 11 月 26 日期间,赞比亚志愿者医护人员使用自我管理的半结构化在线问卷进行了一项全国横断面研究。该研究包括 173 名参与者,旨在评估 HBV 疫苗接种 的摄取及其预测因素。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 R 版本 4.6.0 和 Stata 版本 17 进行描述性统计和推论统计分析数据,并应用小于 0.05 的两侧 p 值阈值以实现统计显着性。使用多变量 Firth 惩罚逻辑回归模型来确定 疫苗接种 摄取的独立预测因子。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 173 名参与者中,51 人(29.5%)报告已接种疫苗;其中,23 人 (45.1%) 接种了一剂疫苗,4 人 (7.8%) 接种了两剂疫苗,24 人 (47.1%) 至少接种了三剂疫苗(完全接种)。培训期间参加 HBV 疫苗接种 计划与 疫苗接种 显着相关 (p < 0.001),卫生机构是否提供 HBV 检测服务也与 疫苗接种 显着相关 (p = 0.006)。年龄的增加也与 疫苗接种 的较高几率相关(p = 0.025),而性别和教育地点在调整后并不独立相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调了赞比亚志愿者医护人员中 HBV 疫苗接种 覆盖率较低,并确定了机构和人口因素(培训期间的 疫苗接种 计划、年龄和现场 HBV 检测服务)作为采用率的关键决定因素。这强调了在培训和基于设施的预防计划中采取有针对性的干预措施的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,在培训期间加强 HBV 疫苗接种 计划并改善获得现场检测服务的机会,可以大幅提高志愿医护人员的 疫苗接种 覆盖率,从而降低赞比亚的职业性 HBV 感染风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 横截面设计限制了因果推断,并且对自我报告的 疫苗接种 状态的依赖可能会引入回忆偏差。173 名参与者的样本量和单一国家背景进一步限制了普遍性,需要谨慎地将证据强度解释为中等。

analysis_en.main_results: Among 173 participants, 51 (29.5%) reported being vaccinated; of these, 23 (45.1%) had received one dose, 4 (7.8%) two doses, and 24 (47.1%) at least three doses (fully vaccinated). analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights low HBV vaccination coverage among volunteer HCWs in Zambia and identifies institutional and demographic factors—vaccination programs during training, age, and on-site HBV testing services—as key determinants of uptake. analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that strengthening HBV vaccination programs during training and improving access to on-site testing services could substantially increase vaccination coverage among volunteer HCWs, thereby reducing occupational HBV infection risk in Zambia.

papers.title_zh: 无人照顾的护理人员:赞比亚志愿医护人员中乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 摄入量和预测因子的横断面研究:志愿医护人员中 HBV 疫苗接种 摄入量。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) poses a major occupational risk to healthcare workers (HCWs), particularly in moderate-to-high‐prevalence settings such as Zambia. Despite the availability of a safe and effective vaccine, coverage among HCWs remains suboptimal. Among HCWs, volunteer HCWs face unique challenges, including financial barriers, that increase their risk. However, they are often overlooked in research. The present study aimed to determine HBV vaccination uptake and its predictors among volunteer HCWs in Zambia. METHODS: This national cross-sectional study utilized a self-administered semi-structured online questionnaire to collect data from volunteer HCWs from October 3 to November 26 2024. Using R version 4.6.0 and Stata version 17, descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were performed. A two-sided p value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. RESULTS: Among the 173 participants, 51 (29.5%) reported being vaccinated. Of the 51, 23 (45.1%) had received one dose, 4 (7.8%) two doses, and 24 (47.1%) at least three doses (fully vaccinated). In the multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression model, participants who had access to HBV vaccination programs during training were significantly more likely to be vaccinated than those without such programs (p < 0.001). Availability of HBV testing services at the health facility was also independently associated with vaccination uptake (p = 0.006). Increasing age was associated with slightly higher odds of vaccination (p = 0.025). Gender and place of education were not independently associated with vaccination uptake after adjustment. CONCLUSION: HBV vaccination coverage among volunteer HCWs in Zambia was low. Vaccination programs during training, age and the availability of HBV testing services were important factors associated with vaccine uptake. Strengthening institutional HBV prevention programs may improve vaccination coverage and reduce occupational risk among HCWs.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景和目标:乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 对医护人员 (HCW) 构成重大职业风险,特别是在赞比亚等中度至高 患病率 环境中。尽管有安全有效的 疫苗,但医护人员的覆盖率仍然不理想。在医护人员中,志愿医护人员面临着独特的挑战,包括财务障碍,这增加了他们的风险。然而,它们在研究中经常被忽视。本研究旨在确定赞比亚志愿医护人员中 HBV 疫苗接种 的摄取情况及其预测因素。方法:这项全国横断面研究采用自我管理的半结构化在线问卷来收集 2024 年 10 月 3 日至 11 月 26 日期间志愿医护人员的数据。使用 R 版本 4.6.0 和 Stata 版本 17 进行描述性和推论统计分析。两侧 p 值 < 0.05 被认为具有统计显着性。结果:在 173 名参与者中,51 人 (29.5%) 报告已接种疫苗。在 51 人中,23 人 (45.1%) 接种了一剂疫苗,4 人 (7.8%) 接种了两剂疫苗,24 人 (47.1%) 至少接种了三剂疫苗(完全接种)。在多变量 Firth 惩罚逻辑回归模型中,在培训期间参与 HBV 疫苗接种 计划的参与者比没有此类计划的参与者更有可能接种疫苗 (p < 0.001)。卫生机构提供的 HBV 检测服务也与 疫苗接种 的吸收率独立相关 (p = 0.006)。年龄的增加与 疫苗接种 的几率稍高相关(p = 0.025)。调整后,性别和教育地点与 疫苗接种 的吸收率没有独立相关。结论:赞比亚志愿医护人员中 HBV 疫苗接种 覆盖率较低。培训期间的 疫苗接种 计划、年龄和 HBV 检测服务的可用性是与 ZX​​QTERMAAQXZ 吸收相关的重要因素。加强机构乙型肝炎预防计划可以提高 疫苗接种 的覆盖率并降低医护人员的职业风险。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 职业接触 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 使医护人员 (HCW) 面临较高的风险,但尽管有安全有效的 疫苗,但 疫苗接种 的覆盖率仍然不理想。志愿医护人员面临着独特的障碍,例如财务限制,并且在研究中经常被忽视,从而造成了关于他们的 疫苗接种 状态和决定因素的知识差距。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024 年 10 月 3 日至 11 月 26 日期间,赞比亚志愿者医护人员使用自我管理的半结构化在线问卷进行了一项全国横断面研究。该研究包括 173 名参与者,旨在评估 HBV 疫苗接种 的摄取及其预测因素。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用 R 版本 4.6.0 和 Stata 版本 17 进行描述性统计和推论统计分析数据,并应用小于 0.05 的两侧 p 值阈值以实现统计显着性。使用多变量 Firth 惩罚逻辑回归模型来确定 疫苗接种 摄取的独立预测因子。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在 173 名参与者中,51 人(29.5%)报告已接种疫苗;其中,23 人 (45.1%) 接种了一剂疫苗,4 人 (7.8%) 接种了两剂疫苗,24 人 (47.1%) 至少接种了三剂疫苗(完全接种)。培训期间参加 HBV 疫苗接种 计划与 疫苗接种 显着相关 (p < 0.001),卫生机构是否提供 HBV 检测服务也与 疫苗接种 显着相关 (p = 0.006)。年龄的增加也与 疫苗接种 的较高几率相关(p = 0.025),而性别和教育地点在调整后并不独立相关。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调了赞比亚志愿者医护人员中 HBV 疫苗接种 覆盖率较低,并确定了机构和人口因素(培训期间的 疫苗接种 计划、年龄和现场 HBV 检测服务)作为采用率的关键决定因素。这强调了在培训和基于设施的预防计划中采取有针对性的干预措施的必要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,在培训期间加强 HBV 疫苗接种 计划并改善获得现场检测服务的机会,可以大幅提高志愿医护人员的 疫苗接种 覆盖率,从而降低赞比亚的职业性 HBV 感染风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 横截面设计限制了因果推断,并且对自我报告的 疫苗接种 状态的依赖可能会引入回忆偏差。173 名参与者的样本量和单一国家背景进一步限制了普遍性,需要谨慎地将证据强度解释为中等。

papers.title: The magnitude of early hepatitis B RNA and DNA declines directly inform capsid assembly modulator effectiveness
papers.abstract: Capsid assembly modulators (CAMs) are a promising class of antiviral treatments for hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. Several CAMs have been evaluated in clinical trials but there is no simple method to estimate their in vivo antiviral effectiveness. We performed viral dynamics modeling of the intracellular and extracellular dynamics of HBV RNA, HBV DNA, and ALT during phase I trials of two CAMs, vebicorvir and ABI-H2158, which inhibit the encapsidation of pgRNA. Fitting our model to the data, we quantify the drug-induced percent inhibition of encapsidated pgRNA production, which we term their in vivo antiviral effectiveness. In both trials, the HBV RNA and HBV DNA declined in a biphasic manner during therapy. The model described these decays well and, by fitting the model to the data, we estimated the CAM effectiveness in each trial participant. Mathematical analysis of the model showed that the magnitude of the first phase of decline of HBV RNA and HBV DNA is explicitly related to CAM effectiveness. However, in the clinic, the end of the first phase may not be known due to sparse sampling. Using clinical trial simulations, we show that the HBV RNA and HBV DNA declines between baseline and day 14 of CAM monotherapy can be used to predict CAM effectiveness. We show that HBV RNA is a clinically relevant biomarker and that very short-term phase I clinical trials can be used to evaluate the in vivo effectiveness of new CAMs, thus reducing the danger of drug resistance developing in trial participants.

papers.title_zh: 早期乙型肝炎 RNA 和 DNA 下降的程度直接影响衣壳组装调节剂的有效性
papers.source_body_en: Capsid assembly modulators (CAMs) are a promising class of antiviral treatments for hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. Several CAMs have been evaluated in clinical trials but there is no simple method to estimate their in vivo antiviral effectiveness. We performed viral dynamics modeling of the intracellular and extracellular dynamics of HBV RNA, HBV DNA, and ALT during phase I trials of two CAMs, vebicorvir and ABI-H2158, which inhibit the encapsidation of pgRNA. Fitting our model to the data, we quantify the drug-induced percent inhibition of encapsidated pgRNA production, which we term their in vivo antiviral effectiveness. In both trials, the HBV RNA and HBV DNA declined in a biphasic manner during therapy. The model described these decays well and, by fitting the model to the data, we estimated the CAM effectiveness in each trial participant. Mathematical analysis of the model showed that the magnitude of the first phase of decline of HBV RNA and HBV DNA is explicitly related to CAM effectiveness. However, in the clinic, the end of the first phase may not be known due to sparse sampling. Using clinical trial simulations, we show that the HBV RNA and HBV DNA declines between baseline and day 14 of CAM monotherapy can be used to predict CAM effectiveness. We show that HBV RNA is a clinically relevant biomarker and that very short-term phase I clinical trials can be used to evaluate the in vivo effectiveness of new CAMs, thus reducing the danger of drug resistance developing in trial participants.
papers.abstract_zh: 衣壳组装调节剂 (CAM) 是一类很有前景的 抗病毒药物 治疗,用于治疗 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染。几种 CAM 已在临床试验中进行了评估,但没有简单的方法来评估它们的体内 抗病毒药物 有效性。在两种 CAM(vebicorvir 和 ABI-H2158)的 I 期试验中,我们对 HBV RNA、HBV DNA 和 ALT 的细胞内和细胞外动力学进行了病毒动力学建模,这两种 CAM 抑制 pgRNA 的衣壳化。将我们的模型与数据进行拟合,我们量化了药物诱导的衣壳化 pgRNA 产生的抑制百分比,我们将其称为体内 抗病毒药物 有效性。在这两项试验中,治疗期间 HBV RNA 和 HBV DNA 均呈双相下降。该模型很好地描述了这些衰减,并且通过将模型与数据进行拟合,我们估计了每个试验参与者的 CAM 有效性。该模型的数学分析表明,HBV RNA 和 HBV DNA 第一阶段下降的幅度与 CAM 有效性明确相关。然而,在临床中,由于采样稀疏,第一阶段的结束可能无法得知。通过临床试验模拟,我们表明,从基线到 CAM 单药治疗第 14 天,HBV RNA 和 HBV DNA 下降,可用于预测 CAM 有效性。我们证明,HBV RNA 是一种临床相关的生物标志物,非常短期的 I 期临床试验可用于评估新 CAM 的体内有效性,从而降低试验参与者产生耐药性的危险。

papers.title: HLA-DQB1*06:02 and a critical amino acid variant in protection against occult hepatitis B virus infection
papers.abstract: The human leukocyte antigen (HLA) system plays a critical role in determining the outcomes of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, yet the genetic mechanisms underlying occult HBV infection (OBI), a form marked by detectable HBV DNA in the absence of hepatitis B surface antigen, remain poorly defined. Here, we performed high-resolution HLA genotyping and amino acid-based association analysis in a Chinese population comprising 239 OBI cases and 545 healthy controls. We identified the HLA class II allele DQB1*06:02 as a protective signal against OBI, with conditional analysis confirming its independent effect. This allele is carried on the conserved haplotype DRB1*15:01~DQA1*02:01~DQB1*06:02, which was significantly underrepresented in OBI cases. Conversely, the DRB1*09:01~DQA1*03:02~DQB1*03:03 haplotype was associated with increased OBI risk. Analysis of the HLA-DQB1 amino acid residues revealed that position 119, located in an α-helix of the peptide-binding groove, drives a substantial portion of the observed association. The phenylalanine variant at this site remained strongly protective after multiple-testing correction and is encoded by DQB1*06:02. Our study thus delineates both allele and amino acid level HLA determinants of OBI susceptibility, highlighting a key structural residue that may influence antigen presentation and immune clearance of HBV. These findings provide a refined genetic framework for understanding host and virus interactions in occult HBV persistence.

papers.title_zh: HLA-DQB1*06:02 和一个关键的氨基酸变体可预防隐匿性 乙型肝炎病毒 感染
papers.source_body_en: The human leukocyte antigen (HLA) system plays a critical role in determining the outcomes of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, yet the genetic mechanisms underlying occult HBV infection (OBI), a form marked by detectable HBV DNA in the absence of hepatitis B surface antigen, remain poorly defined. Here, we performed high-resolution HLA genotyping and amino acid-based association analysis in a Chinese population comprising 239 OBI cases and 545 healthy controls. We identified the HLA class II allele DQB1*06:02 as a protective signal against OBI, with conditional analysis confirming its independent effect. This allele is carried on the conserved haplotype DRB1*15:01~DQA1*02:01~DQB1*06:02, which was significantly underrepresented in OBI cases. Conversely, the DRB1*09:01~DQA1*03:02~DQB1*03:03 haplotype was associated with increased OBI risk. Analysis of the HLA-DQB1 amino acid residues revealed that position 119, located in an α-helix of the peptide-binding groove, drives a substantial portion of the observed association. The phenylalanine variant at this site remained strongly protective after multiple-testing correction and is encoded by DQB1*06:02. Our study thus delineates both allele and amino acid level HLA determinants of OBI susceptibility, highlighting a key structural residue that may influence antigen presentation and immune clearance of HBV. These findings provide a refined genetic framework for understanding host and virus interactions in occult HBV persistence.
papers.abstract_zh: 人类白细胞抗原 (HLA) 系统在确定 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染的结果中发挥着关键作用,但隐匿性 HBV 感染 (OBI) 的遗传机制仍不清楚,隐匿性 HBV 感染 (OBI) 是一种在没有乙型肝炎表面抗原的情况下以可检测到的 HBV DNA 为标志的形式。在这里,我们对包括 239 名 OBI 病例和 545 名健康对照的中国人群进行了高分辨率 HLA 基因分型和基于氨基酸的关联分析。我们将 HLA II 类等位基因 DQB1*06:02 确定为针对 OBI 的保护信号,条件分析证实了其独立作用。该等位基因携带保守的单倍型 DRB1*15:01~DQA1*02:01~DQB1*06:02,在 OBI 病例中明显不足。相反,DRB1*09:01~DQA1*03:02~DQB1*03:03 单倍型与 OBI 风险增加相关。对 HLA-DQB1 氨基酸残基的分析表明,位于肽结合沟 α 螺旋中的位置 119 驱动了所观察到的关联的很大一部分。该位点的苯丙氨酸变体经过多重测试校正后仍然具有很强的保护性,由DQB1*06:02编码。因此,我们的研究描绘了 OBI 易感性的等位基因和氨基酸水平 HLA 决定因素,强调了可能影响 HBV 抗原呈递和免疫清除的关键结构残基。这些发现为理解 宿主 和隐匿性 HBV 持续存在中的病毒相互作用提供了一个完善的遗传框架。

papers.title: Drug resistance mutations of hepatitis B virus (HBV) influence the yield of the virions of the human hepatitis delta virus (HDV) and their infectivity
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This work analyzed 30 drug resistance mutations (DRMs) in the surface antigen of hepatitis B virus (HBV) (i.e., HBsAg) selected by several FDA-approved anti-HBV nucleos(t)ide analogs. All DRM-bearing HBsAg variants supported the formation and secretion of hepatitis delta virus (HDV), and only 13/30 DRMs considerably decreased the yield of secreted HDV virions. However, the majority of DRMs (23/30) greatly reduced HDV infectivity, and four of them even caused the complete loss of infectivity, which was determined by analyzing the levels of HDV RNA genomes in the infected cells, and the fraction of HDV-infected cells. The ability to inhibit HDV infectivity was observed for DRMs located in the large cytosolic loop (LCL), major antigenic loop (MAL), HDV-binding site (HDV-BS), and the transmembrane domains II, III, and IV of HBsAg, which suggested that DRMs mediate their inhibitory influence by both direct and indirect mechanisms that could alter the attachment/entry, post-entry trafficking, and/or subsequent uncoating of the virions. This report also established the transmembrane domains II, III, and IV as critical regulators of the overall infectivity of HDV virions. It became apparent that in the settings of natural HBV/HDV infection, DRMs can therefore greatly reduce the spread/superinfection of HDV and diminish the size of the HDV reservoir in chronically infected livers. Overall, our findings advanced the understanding of how anti-HBV drug treatments influence the HDV life cycle, the roles of HBV envelope proteins in facilitating the assembly and infectivity of HDV, and the mechanism of complex HBV-HDV interactions. IMPORTANCE The study showed that the drug resistance mutations (DRMs) in the surface antigen of hepatitis B virus (HBsAg) can greatly reduce hepatitis delta virus (HDV) assembly and infectivity. Since most of the tested DRMs considerably reduced HDV infectivity, and four of them resulted in a complete loss of the infectivity, such effects can lead to suppression of HDV spread/superinfection and reduction of the HDV reservoir in the infected liver. If most detrimental for infectivity DRMs are present on the majority of HBsAg molecules, this could facilitate substantial suppression of chronic HDV infection and possibly reduce HDV-associated liver pathogenesis. It was also determined that DRMs located in the transmembrane domains II, III, and IV of HBsAg could critically alter HDV infectivity. Our findings therefore suggest that different HBsAg regions work in the intramolecular coordinating concert, facilitating the assembly and infectivity of the virions, and that certain short- and long-distance interactions between different regions of HBsAg take place.

All DRM-bearing HBsAg variants supported the formation and secretion of hepatitis delta virus (HDV), and only 13/30 DRMs considerably decreased the yield of secreted HDV virions. However, the majority of DRMs (23/30) greatly reduced HDV infectivity, and four of them even caused the complete loss of infectivity, which was determined by analyzing the levels of HDV RNA genomes in the infected cells, and the fraction of HDV-infected cells. The ability to inhibit HDV infectivity was observed for DRMs located in the large cytosolic loop (LCL), major antigenic loop (MAL), HDV-binding site (HDV-BS), and the transmembrane domains II, III, and IV of HBsAg, which suggested that DRMs mediate their inhibitory influence by both direct and indirect mechanisms that could alter the attachment/entry, post-entry trafficking, and/or subsequent uncoating of the virions. This report also established the transmembrane domains II, III, and IV as critical regulators of the overall infectivity of HDV virions. It became apparent that in the settings of natural HBV/HDV infection, DRMs can therefore greatly reduce the spread/superinfection of HDV and diminish the size of the HDV reservoir in chronically infected livers. Overall, our findings advanced the understanding of how anti-HBV drug treatments influence the HDV life cycle, the roles of HBV envelope proteins in facilitating the assembly and infectivity of HDV, and the mechanism of complex HBV-HDV interactions. IMPORTANCE The study showed that the drug resistance mutations (DRMs) in the surface antigen of hepatitis B virus (HBsAg) can greatly reduce hepatitis delta virus (HDV) assembly and infectivity. Since most of the tested DRMs considerably reduced HDV infectivity, and four of them resulted in a complete loss of the infectivity, such effects can lead to suppression of HDV spread/superinfection and reduction of the HDV reservoir in the infected liver. If most detrimental for infectivity DRMs are present on the majority of HBsAg molecules, this could facilitate substantial suppression of chronic HDV infection and possibly reduce HDV-associated liver pathogenesis. It was also determined that DRMs located in the transmembrane domains II, III, and IV of HBsAg could critically alter HDV infectivity. Our findings therefore suggest that different HBsAg regions work in the intramolecular coordinating concert, facilitating the assembly and infectivity of the virions, and that certain short- and long-distance interactions between different regions of HBsAg take place.

papers.title_original: Drug resistance mutations of hepatitis B virus (HBV) influence the yield of the virions of the human hepatitis delta virus (HDV) and their infectivity

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate how drug resistance mutations (DRMs) in the surface antigen of hepatitis B virus (HBV) affect the assembly and infectivity of hepatitis delta virus (HDV). The background highlights the importance of understanding these interactions to improve therapeutic strategies for HBV/HDV co-infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed 30 DRMs in HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) selected by FDA-approved anti-HBV nucleos(t)ide analogs. These DRMs were tested for their impact on HDV assembly and infectivity in a controlled experimental setting.
analysis.methods: The researchers examined the ability of DRM-bearing HBsAg variants to support HDV formation and secretion by analyzing HDV RNA genome levels and the fraction of HDV-infected cells. They also identified the specific regions of HBsAg where DRMs exerted their effects.
analysis.main_results: All DRM-bearing HBsAg variants supported HDV formation and secretion, but only 13/30 DRMs significantly reduced the yield of secreted HDV virions. Additionally, 23/30 DRMs greatly reduced HDV infectivity, with four causing a complete loss of infectivity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that DRMs in specific regions of HBsAg can inhibit HDV infectivity through direct and indirect mechanisms, altering virion attachment/entry, trafficking, and uncoating. They also identified transmembrane domains II, III, and IV as critical regulators of HDV infectivity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that anti-HBV drug treatments may influence HDV life cycle and reduce HDV spread/superinfection, potentially leading to a decrease in HDV-associated liver pathogenesis in chronically infected individuals.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to an abstract-only analysis, and the evidence is based on experimental observations of DRM effects on HDV. The confidence in these findings is moderate due to the lack of detailed experimental data and broader clinical validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how drug resistance mutations (DRMs) in the surface antigen of hepatitis B virus (HBV) affect the assembly and infectivity of hepatitis delta virus (HDV). The research analyzed 30 DRMs selected by FDA-approved anti-HBV drugs and found that while all DRM-bearing HBsAg variants supported HDV formation, only 13/30 DRMs significantly reduced HDV virion yield. Moreover, 23/30 DRMs greatly reduced HDV infectivity, with four causing complete loss of infectivity. The authors suggest that DRMs may alter HDV infectivity through direct and indirect mechanisms, affecting virion attachment, trafficking, and uncoating. They also identified transmembrane domains II, III, and IV of HBsAg as critical regulators of HDV infectivity. These findings highlight the potential of anti-HBV treatments to suppress HDV spread and reduce liver pathogenesis. However, the study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the results need further experimental and clinical validation to establish their broader implications.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)表面抗原中的耐药性乙型肝炎病毒(DRM)如何影响丁型肝炎病毒(HDV)的组装和感染性。这一背景强调了了解这些相互作用对于改善 HBV/HDV 合并感染的治疗策略的重要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了由 FDA 批准的抗 HBV 核苷类似物选择的 HBV 表面抗原 (HBsAg) 中的 30 种 DRM。在受控实验环境中测试了这些 DRM 对 HDV 组装和感染性的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员通过分析 HDV RNA 基因组 水平和 HDV 感染细胞的比例,检查了带有 DRM 的 HBsAg 变体支持 HDV 形成和分泌的能力。他们还确定了 DRM 发挥作用的 HBsAg 特定区域。
elements_zh.main_results: 所有携带 DRM 的 HBsAg 变体都支持 HDV 的形成和分泌,但只有 13/30 DRM 显着降低了分泌的 HDV 病毒体的产量。此外,23/30 DRM 大大降低了丁型肝炎病毒的感染性,其中 4 个 DRM 导致感染性完全丧失。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,HBsAg 特定区域的 DRM 可以通过直接和间接机制抑制 HDV 感染性,改变病毒粒子的附着/进入、运输和脱壳。他们还确定跨膜结构域 II、III 和 IV 是 HDV 感染性的关键调节因子。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,抗 HBV 药物 治疗 可能会影响 HDV 生命周期并减少 HDV 传播/重复感染,可能导致慢性感染个体中 HDV 相关肝脏 发病机制 减少。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于抽象分析,证据基于 DRM 对 HDV 影响的实验观察。由于缺乏详细的实验数据和更广泛的临床验证,这些发现的可信度较低。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 这项工作分析了由 FDA 批准的几种抗 HBV 核苷类似物选择的 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 表面抗原(即 HBsAg)中的 30 种耐药性 突变 (DRM)。所有携带 DRM 的 HBsAg 变体都支持丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 的形成和分泌,只有 13/30 DRM 显着降低了分泌的 HDV 病毒粒子的产量。然而,大多数DRM(23/30)大大降低了HDV的感染性,其中四种甚至导致感染性完全丧失,这是通过分析感染细胞中HDV RNA 基因组的水平以及HDV感染细胞的比例来确定的。观察到位于大胞质环 (LCL)、主要抗原环 (MAL)、HDV 结合位点 (HDV-BS) 和 HBsAg 跨膜结构域 II、III 和 IV 中的 DRM 具有抑制 HDV 感染性的能力,这表明 DRM 通过直接和间接机制介导其抑制影响,这些机制可能改变病毒粒子的附着/进入、进入后运输和/或随后的脱壳。该报告还确立了跨膜结构域 II、III 和 IV 作为 HDV 病毒粒子整体感染性的关键调节因子。很明显,在自然 HBV/HDV 感染的情况下,DRM 可以大大减少 HDV 的传播/重复感染,并缩小慢性感染肝脏中 HDV 储存宿主 的大小。总体而言,我们的研究结果加深了对抗 HBV 药物 治疗 如何影响 HDV 生命周期、HBV 包膜蛋白在促进 HDV 组装和感染性中的作用以及复杂 HBV-HDV 相互作用机制的理解。重要性 研究表明,乙型肝炎病毒(HBsAg)表面抗原中的耐药性突变(DRMs)可以大大降低丁型肝炎病毒(HDV)的组装和传染性。由于大多数测试的 DRM 显着降低了 HDV 感染性,其中四种导致感染性完全丧失,因此这种作用可以抑制 HDV 传播/重复感染,并减少受感染肝脏中的 HDV 储存宿主。如果对感染性最有害的 DRM 存在于大多数 HBsAg 分子上,这可能有助于显着抑制慢性 HDV 感染,并可能减少 HDV 相关肝脏 发病机制。还确定位于 HBsAg 跨膜域 II、III 和 IV 中的 DRM 可以严重改变 HDV 感染性。因此,我们的研究结果表明,不同的 HBsAg 区域在分子内协调作用中发挥作用,促进病毒体的组装和感染性,并且 HBsAg 不同区域之间发生某些短距离和长距离相互作用。

papers.title: Nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy combined with pegylated interferon α-2b guided by the GOLDEN prediction model for functional cure of chronic hepatitis B: study protocol (GIFT project).
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The limited efficacy and tolerability of interferon (IFN)-based therapies make refining patient selection a critical step towards achieving a functional cure in chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The novel GOLDEN model, based on sequential changes in quantitative HBsAg (qHBsAg), accurately predicts hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss in patients with CHB receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy. However, it remains unvalidated in patients receiving sequential pegylated IFN α-2b (Peg-IFN α-2b)-based therapy. We aim to validate the GOLDEN model and the optimised cut-off value for the predictive index (Pi) to prospectively identify optimal candidates for clinical cure among patients receiving sequential Peg-IFN α-2b therapy using pre-IFN treatment qHBsAg kinetics across multiple centres. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This prospective multicentre observational cohort study will enrol 300 NA-experienced patients with CHB from 22 centres in China. Patients, stratified by the Pi calculated from pre-treatment qHBsAg dynamics, will be classified into two groups: favourable (Pi>0.15, n=150) and unfavourable candidates (Pi≤0.15, n=150). All patients will receive 48 weeks of combination therapy with Peg-IFN α-2b plus ongoing NAs. The primary endpoint is the HBsAg clearance rate at week 48, with clearance defined as HBsAg loss at any time during the treatment period. Secondary endpoints include HBsAg seroconversion and sustained clearance rates. The sample size provides 80% power to detect a significant difference between the assumed clearance rates (35% vs 20%, favourable vs unfavourable group). Between-group comparisons will be performed using the χ2 or Fisher's exact test. Long-term follow-up studies are warranted to assess sustained HBsAg clearance and its impact on clinical outcomes. Concurrently, we will explore establishing novel predictive models using this framework alongside other baseline indicators. Future research could focus on analysing serial inflammatory cytokine profiles from stored blood samples to elucidate the immunological mechanisms driving treatment response. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study protocol has been reviewed, and ethical approval has been obtained from the ethics committee of Tangdu Hospital, Fourth Military Medical University (approval no. Approval has also been secured from 21 additional participating centres. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ChiCTR2500095819.

analysis.summary_en: This study protocol outlines a prospective multicentre observational cohort study aimed at validating the GOLDEN prediction model for identifying optimal candidates for a functional cure in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) using nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy combined with pegylated interferon α-2b (Peg-IFN α-2b). The study will enrol 300 NA-experienced patients with CHB from 22 centres in China, stratified into favourable (Pi>0.15) and unfavourable (Pi≤0.15) groups based on pre-treatment quantitative HBsAg (qHBsAg) dynamics. The primary endpoint is HBsAg clearance at week 48, with secondary endpoints including HBsAg seroconversion and sustained clearance rates. The study will use χ2 or Fisher's exact tests for between-group comparisons and aims to provide 80% power to detect a significant difference between clearance rates (35% vs 20%). The GOLDEN model, which uses sequential qHBsAg changes, is interpreted as accurately predicting HBsAg loss in CHB patients on NA therapy. The findings may inform improved patient selection strategies for combination therapy. However, the study is limited to a single model and lacks long-term follow-up data, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过验证 GOLDEN 预测模型来完善患者选择,以实现 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 中的 功能性治愈,该模型使用定量 HBsAg (qHBsAg) 动力学来识别最佳治疗候选者。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项前瞻性多中心观察性 队列研究 研究,招募了来自中国 22 个中心的 300 名有 NA 经验的 CHB 患者。根据 治疗 前 qHBsAg 动态计算得出的预测指数 (Pi) 将患者分为两组:有利候选者 (Pi>0.15,n=150) 和不利候选者 (Pi≤0.15,n=150)。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究将对 48 周以上的所有患者使用 Peg-IFN α-2b 加持续核苷(酸)类似物 (NA) 的联合疗法。组间比较将使用 χ2 或 Fisher 精确检验进行。
elements_zh.main_results: 主要终点是第 48 周时的 HBsAg 清除率,清除率定义为 治疗 期间任何时间的 HBsAg 消失。样本量提供 80% 的功效来检测假设清除率之间的显着差异(35% 与 20%,有利组与不利组)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: GOLDEN 模型基于 qHBsAg 的连续变化,可以准确预测接受 NA 治疗的慢性乙型肝炎患者的 HBsAg 消失。该研究将探索使用该框架和其他基线指标建立新颖的预测模型。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为制定更有效的策略来选择患者进行联合治疗提供信息,从而有可能提高在 慢性乙型肝炎 中实现 功能性治愈 的可能性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单一预测模型,不包括长期随访数据。证据是中等的,因为它基于具有明确样本量和统计分析的前瞻性观察设计。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过验证 GOLDEN 预测模型来完善患者选择,以实现 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 中的 功能性治愈,该模型使用定量 HBsAg (qHBsAg) 动力学来识别最佳治疗候选者。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项前瞻性多中心观察性 队列研究 研究,招募了来自中国 22 个中心的 300 名有 NA 经验的 CHB 患者。根据 治疗 前 qHBsAg 动态计算得出的预测指数 (Pi) 将患者分为两组:有利候选者 (Pi>0.15,n=150) 和不利候选者 (Pi≤0.15,n=150)。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究将对 48 周以上的所有患者使用 Peg-IFN α-2b 加持续核苷(酸)类似物 (NA) 的联合疗法。组间比较将使用 χ2 或 Fisher 精确检验进行。
analysis_zh.main_results: 主要终点是第 48 周时的 HBsAg 清除率,清除率定义为 治疗 期间任何时间的 HBsAg 消失。样本量提供 80% 的功效来检测假设清除率之间的显着差异(35% 与 20%,有利组与不利组)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: GOLDEN 模型基于 qHBsAg 的连续变化,可以准确预测接受 NA 治疗的慢性乙型肝炎患者的 HBsAg 消失。该研究将探索使用该框架和其他基线指标建立新颖的预测模型。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为制定更有效的策略来选择患者进行联合治疗提供信息,从而有可能提高在 慢性乙型肝炎 中实现 功能性治愈 的可能性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单一预测模型,不包括长期随访数据。证据是中等的,因为它基于具有明确样本量和统计分析的前瞻性观察设计。

papers.title: Dynamics on Hepatitis B Virus Infection In Vivo with Immune Noise and Interval Delay
papers.abstract: Immune delay and noise are ubiquitous in the evolution of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in vivo . A stochastic HBV infection dynamic model is proposed to investigate the interaction effects of interval delay and white noise during the immune phase. Global existence, nonnegativity, and boundedness of the solutions are obtained. The stochastic reproduction number is derived, which serves as a threshold determining viral extinction or persistence within-host. Furthermore, the stability conditions for the first and second moments are established. Numerical simulations, employing time-series analysis, confirm the existence of stochastic periodicity. Compared to the deterministic model, noise induces an earlier onset of stochastic periodicity. However, based on the expectation stability of the sample trajectories, as the Hopf bifurcation of the corresponding deterministic system has not yet occurred, the noise-induced early periodicity is likely a temporary phenomenon rather than a true periodic behavior.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the impact of immune delay and noise on HBV infection dynamics in vivo, as these factors are ubiquitous in the evolution of HBV infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A stochastic HBV infection dynamic model was proposed to investigate the interaction effects of interval delay and white noise during the immune phase. The model focuses on human hepatitis B virus infection and its in vivo dynamics.
analysis.methods: Global existence, nonnegativity, and boundedness of the solutions were obtained through mathematical analysis. The stochastic reproduction number was derived as a threshold for determining viral extinction or persistence within-host. Numerical simulations using time-series analysis were conducted to confirm the existence of stochastic periodicity.
analysis.main_results: The stability conditions for the first and second moments were established. Numerical simulations confirmed the existence of stochastic periodicity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that noise induces an earlier onset of stochastic periodicity compared to the deterministic model. This finding highlights the role of immune noise in shaping HBV infection dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more accurate models for HBV infection dynamics, which may aid in understanding the mechanisms of viral persistence and the design of targeted interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a mathematical model and does not involve empirical data. The evidence is abstract-only, and the confidence in the findings is moderate due to the lack of direct experimental validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the dynamics of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in vivo, focusing on the effects of immune delay and noise. A stochastic model was developed to analyze the interaction of interval delay and white noise during the immune phase. The model established global existence, nonnegativity, and boundedness of solutions, derived a stochastic reproduction number as a threshold for viral extinction or persistence, and confirmed the existence of stochastic periodicity through numerical simulations. The authors interpreted that immune noise leads to an earlier onset of stochastic periodicity compared to deterministic models, suggesting that noise plays a significant role in HBV infection dynamics. The findings have implications for improving models of HBV infection and understanding viral persistence mechanisms. However, the study is based on a mathematical model without empirical data, limiting the confidence in its conclusions to a moderate level.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解免疫延迟和噪音对体内 HBV 感染动态的影响,因为这些因素在 HBV 感染的 进化 中普遍存在。

elements_zh.methods: 通过数学分析得到解的全局存在性、非负性和有界性。得出随机繁殖数作为确定 宿主 内病毒灭绝或持续存在的阈值。使用时间序列分析进行数值模拟以确认随机周期性的存在。
elements_zh.main_results: 建立了第一、二阶矩的稳定条件。数值模拟证实了随机周期性的存在。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,与确定性模型相比,噪声会导致随机周期性更早出现。这一发现凸显了免疫噪音在塑造乙型肝炎病毒感染动态中的作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发更准确的乙型肝炎病毒感染动态模型提供信息,这可能有助于了解病毒持续存在的机制和有针对性的干预措施的设计。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于数学模型,不涉及经验数据。证据仅是抽象的,由于缺乏直接的实验验证,研究结果的可信度较低。

analysis_zh.main_results: 建立了第一、二阶矩的稳定条件。数值模拟证实了随机周期性的存在。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,与确定性模型相比,噪声会导致随机周期性更早出现。这一发现凸显了免疫噪音在塑造乙型肝炎病毒感染动态中的作用。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发更准确的乙型肝炎病毒感染动态模型提供信息,这可能有助于了解病毒持续存在的机制和有针对性的干预措施的设计。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于数学模型,不涉及经验数据。证据仅是抽象的,由于缺乏直接的实验验证,研究结果的可信度较低。

papers.title: Global stability of two-patch within-host HBV infection dynamics with unidirectional viral spread
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infects liver cells (hepatocytes). Persistent HBV infection may lead to the development of abnormal nodular formations within liver tissue. In this study, we propose and analyze a mathematical model describing the dynamics of a two-patch within-host HBV infection with unidirectional viral transmission from patch-1 to patch-2. The model captures interactions among six compartments: uninfected hepatocytes, infected hepatocytes, and free HBV particles in each of the two patches. A comprehensive mathematical analysis is carried out, including proofs of non-negativity and boundedness of solutions. The basic reproduction numbers in patch-1 \(\left(R_{1}\right)\) and patch-2 \(\left(R_{2}\right)\) are calculated using the next generation method. The global stability of all equilibrium points is rigorously examined using Lyapunov functions and LaSalle’s invariance principle. Numerical simulations are conducted, demonstrating strong agreement with the analytical findings. Finally, sensitivity analysis identifies the key parameters influencing viral persistence.
papers.journal: International Journal of Analysis and Applications
